root_cause: Production public.brain_observe_failure overwrote aggregate JSON evidence with coalesce(p_evidence,evidence), erasing prior promoted proof keys from its summary. Independently, different agents recorded one cron.runid under both cron-46:RUNID and supabase:cron:job46:run:RUNID, inflating raw occurrence_count by event aliasing (20 raw rows vs 11 distinct provider run IDs on 2026-10-22).
impact: Cumulative learning evidence can be silently lost and dashboards can overcount material incidents, defeating autonomous learning/reuse and recurrence prediction.

source_evidence.source_contract: SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public, only service_role EXECUTE; raw occurrences remain immutable

prevention_rule: Resolve one canonical provider-event ID before writing and serialize all old aliases with one transaction-scoped lock; if payload hashes or fingerprints differ, fail closed and investigate rather than coerce them. Preserve all previously promoted evidence keys; append compact immutable event pointers while raw payloads remain in brain_failure_occurrences. Never delete historical duplicate raw records or add another scheduler/registry.
recovery: Protected SQL migration updates existing brain_observe_failure only, retaining signature, privilege and search path; known cron aliases normalize to project/jobid/runid, and summary evidence is append-only rather than wholesale replaced. No production DDL before isolated database acceptance.
regression_contract: two alias IDs same hash count once
two alias IDs different hashes fail closed
next_action: Execute SQL integration tests in an independently isolated preview, prove ACL/hash-conflict/concurrent writes with production-like function, verify Required/CodeQL/provider and exact main readback before claiming PROD GREEN.
